2026 General Election Voter Guide

Actual Article Body:
voter guide

Enter your address and make more informed decisions. It’s that simple with The Salt Lake Tribune’s 2026 voter guide.

Utahns will choose the winners of more than 80 seats in the Utah Legislature, congressional seats and more, along with deciding on ballot measures. Submitting your address will connect you to the races on your ballot that have a Tribune guide.

Election Day is Nov. 3. If you’re voting by mail, your ballot either needs to be in a drop box or your county clerk’s possession by 8 p.m. on Election Day.

A few easy steps you can take before Election Day

0 of 3 done

Make sure you’re registered to vote, find your polling location or update your voter information. Online registration closes Oct. 23. After that, you can still register in person when you vote.

Deadline Friday, Oct. 23 · Google / Apple/Outlook calendar

Enter your information to find locations for drop boxes and polling places.

Sign up for ballot notifications and check your ballot status.

Deadline Tuesday, Nov. 3 · Google / Apple/Outlook calendar

It’s not easy to cut through all the noise of an election cycle.

All so you, and your neighbors, can make choices with confidence.

Election countdown: Steve Hilton talks jobs, Xavier Becerra hangs with LGBTQ leaders with 4 days to go

With four days to go until the election, Steve Hilton is targeting homelessness and California’s high cost of living in Sacramento, while Xavier Becerra meets with LGBTQ+ leaders in San Francisco.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

With four days to go until the election, Steve Hilton targeted homelessness and California’s high cost of living in Sacramento, while Xavier Becerra met with LGBTQ+ leaders in San Francisco.

The Republican and Democratic rivals made their closing pitches Friday ahead of the campaign’s final weekend, with Hilton planning a three-stop swing through the capital and Becerra preparing to campaign alongside a roster of Democratic allies.

Becerra joined San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie at a Friday morning reception, before heading south to share the stage with Gov. Gavin Newsom on Sunday at Hollywood’s Palladium.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Never miss a story

The final push follows another round of sparring over affordability, after Hilton attacked Becerra on Thursday for leaving open the possibility of a mileage tax during a KCRA interview.

“As governor, I will veto the mileage tax,” Hilton told The California Post.

Becerra’s campaign pushed back against suggestions that he had embraced the idea.

“Secretary Becerra has not proposed a mileage tax,” campaign spokesperson Jonathan Underland told The Post.

Becerra’s Thursday schedule also included an appearance at Los Angeles’ Grand Central Market, a get-out-the-vote event and business walk with Assemblymember Celeste Rodriguez, a CHIRLA Action Fund phone bank and a reception with Asian American and Pacific Islander community leaders.

California Post News: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, WhatsApp, LinkedInCalifornia Post Sports Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, XCalifornia Post  Opinion California Post Newsletters: Sign up here!California Post App: Download here!Home delivery: Sign up here!Page Six Hollywood: Sign up here!

Hilton brought his affordability argument to the governor’s backyard, pairing criticism of Democratic leadership with proposals on job training and homelessness.

His first stop is the California Construction College Academy, where he is scheduled to announce a plan to expand hands-on training in construction, manufacturing and engineering.

His campaign says the proposal would help young people find good-paying jobs while addressing workforce shortages.

Later in the afternoon, Hilton is scheduled to visit Loaves & Fishes to announce a homelessness plan his campaign says would deliver “more effective solutions” that improve public safety and help people get off the streets.

He will finish the day with a 5:30 p.m. rally at Cal Expo focused on the cost of living and pressures facing Sacramento-area families after 16 years of Democratic governors.

Becerra’s Friday schedule began with a San Francisco reception, and his weekend itinerary will take him from the Central Valley to Southern California.

On Saturday, Becerra is scheduled to campaign in Modesto with Democratic Rep. Adam Gray. Becerra will then travel to Oceanside for a Sunday appearance with Democratic officials and candidates, including state Senate leader Monique Limón, Sen. Catherine Blakespear and Assembly candidate Mara Elliott.

Becerra is then scheduled to join Democratic Rep. Dave Min in Irvine that afternoon before heading to Los Angeles for the 4 p.m. rally with Newsom.

The “Stop the Power Grab” event at the Hollywood Palladium will focus on the approaching election and key contests up and down the ballot.

With four days to go until the election, Steve Hilton targeted homelessness and California’s high cost of living in Sacramento, while Xavier Becerra met with LGBTQ+ leaders in San Francisco.

The Republican and Democratic rivals made their closing pitches Friday ahead of the campaign’s final weekend, with Hilton planning a three-stop swing through the capital and Becerra preparing to campaign alongside a roster of Democratic allies.

Becerra joined San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie at a Friday morning reception, before heading south to share the stage with Gov. Gavin Newsom on Sunday at Hollywood’s Palladium.

The final push follows another round of sparring over affordability, after Hilton attacked Becerra on Thursday for leaving open the possibility of a mileage tax during a KCRA interview.

“As governor, I will veto the mileage tax,” Hilton told The California Post.

Becerra’s campaign pushed back against suggestions that he had embraced the idea.

“Secretary Becerra has not proposed a mileage tax,” campaign spokesperson Jonathan Underland told The Post.

Becerra’s Thursday schedule also included an appearance at Los Angeles’ Grand Central Market, a get-out-the-vote event and business walk with Assemblymember Celeste Rodriguez, a CHIRLA Action Fund phone bank and a reception with Asian American and Pacific Islander community leaders.

Hilton brought his affordability argument to the governor’s backyard, pairing criticism of Democratic leadership with proposals on job training and homelessness.

His first stop is the California Construction College Academy, where he is scheduled to announce a plan to expand hands-on training in construction, manufacturing and engineering.

His campaign says the proposal would help young people find good-paying jobs while addressing workforce shortages.

Later in the afternoon, Hilton is scheduled to visit Loaves & Fishes to announce a homelessness plan his campaign says would deliver “more effective solutions” that improve public safety and help people get off the streets.

He will finish the day with a 5:30 p.m. rally at Cal Expo focused on the cost of living and pressures facing Sacramento-area families after 16 years of Democratic governors.

Becerra’s Friday schedule began with a San Francisco reception, and his weekend itinerary will take him from the Central Valley to Southern California.

On Saturday, Becerra is scheduled to campaign in Modesto with Democratic Rep. Adam Gray. Becerra will then travel to Oceanside for a Sunday appearance with Democratic officials and candidates, including state Senate leader Monique Limón, Sen. Catherine Blakespear and Assembly candidate Mara Elliott.

Becerra is then scheduled to join Democratic Rep. Dave Min in Irvine that afternoon before heading to Los Angeles for the 4 p.m. rally with Newsom.

The “Stop the Power Grab” event at the Hollywood Palladium will focus on the approaching election and key contests up and down the ballot.
